# Sampark India Logistics Limited
## 1. Executive Verdict

Sampark is an established, predominantly domestic B2B freight coordinator with road, air and rail capabilities, leased warehousing and small emerging international/umbrella services. Its operating margins have improved, but the central investment question is whether invoiced and unbilled revenue can become cash without consuming repeated fresh capital. FY26 revenue was ₹223.2664 crore and operating EBITDA ₹20.0143 crore, yet CFO was only ₹1.8129 crore and genuinely unrestricted cash approximately ₹0.6720 crore. The July 2026 IPO provides meaningful working-capital relief, not proof of a completed improvement in collection economics. Historical BQS is 4.92 (displayed 4.9); raw GQS is 5.35, capped at 5.0 because CASH is 3. IAS remains NS because a supported forward return, price-implied expectation and primary liquidity assessment are unresolved. This is a mixed-quality, cash-constrained logistics watchlist case, not an evidence-backed compounder or an evidenced governance/default failure. At the secondary 19 October close of ₹141.50, valuation work is conditional. Better collections, documented IPO deployment, bank availability and an executable primary trade record could change the assessment. [A04,A06,C01–C04,L01]

## 4. Business Overview

The operating proposition is coordination and service reliability: collect B2B consignments, consolidate and route them through carriers and branch infrastructure, deliver to the consignee, obtain proof/acceptance, invoice and collect. Sampark offers FTL/LTL road movement, air and rail forwarding, warehousing, inventory handling and packaging. Its prospectus records 50 branches, 56 owned vehicles, and eight leased warehouses totalling 124,500 square feet. Hired pickup/delivery and external carriers are economically important, so owned-vehicle count is not total throughput capacity. Office and warehouse rent stays in operating cost under this Indian GAAP presentation; no invented Ind AS lease liability is added. [B01,B02]

FY26 note 17 reconciles ₹223.2664 crore revenue as net billed freight ₹195.1314 crore, warehousing ₹7.5811 crore, truck/GPS rental ₹0.0007 crore, current unbilled freight ₹18.8828 crore and umbrella supplier revenue ₹1.6704 crore. Gross freight ₹208.7094 crore first reverses prior unbilled ₹13.5780 crore. Therefore ₹18.8828 crore is not all incremental recognition: the net annual unbilled addition is ₹5.3048 crore. The December-to-March fall in the unbilled balance is not automatically cash collection; it can be invoicing or other movement. [B03; FY26 annual printed 65/PDF69]

The older prospectus describes domestic B2B logistics, but FY26 adds international freight and umbrella services. Foreign-exchange umbrella income is ₹1.6703 crore and freight income ₹0.0053 crore; the directors’ total differs by ₹0.0001 crore rounding. “100% domestic” is therefore not carried forward. Current international activity remains small; it is not evidence of a broad international franchise. A single reportable segment is an accounting disclosure, not proof of identical service-level margins. [B01,B03]

Revenue recognition is a FY26 key audit matter. Delivery/control transfer and service performance underpin recognition; invoice approval and customer reconciliation affect timing. There is a genuine sequence from service delivery to billing to collection, and the model keeps billed/unbilled movements separate. Carrier costs and payroll can precede cash receipts, explaining why an apparently asset-light coordinator can be intensely working-capital dependent. [A01,A04,M01]

## 5. Moat / Industry Position

The best proposed mechanism is local network knowledge and integrated customer service: routes, carrier relationships and branch execution can reduce coordination friction. Evidence is a meaningful operating footprint and repeated activity over more than a decade. Durability depends on service retention, route density, passing through freight costs and billing discipline. Failure modes are price-based tender competition, carrier repricing, customer switching and funding an ever-larger debtor book. Neither ISO certification, GPS, reputed customer logos nor high reported ROCE proves a moat. The issuer itself describes fragmented competition and low barriers, and relies on third-party technology and capacity. Proprietary technology is not established. [B01,B02]

Customer concentration is real but not one-customer dependence: FY25 top customer represented 7.82% and top ten 38.72% of sales; nine-month FY26 top customer 9.56%, top ten 34.34%. Supplier concentration is greater: FY25 top supplier 32.23% and top ten 64.17% of operating procurement expenses. These are different denominators. Names of the latest top supplier/customer are not disclosed in those tables. Fretex matches the FY23/FY24 top-customer amounts, ₹16.3136/₹22.6181 crore, when it was related. Nil later related-party sales is not proof sales ceased after its relationship changed. [B02,B03]

## 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway

A bottom-up scale test starts with the existing 50-branch/56-owned-vehicle/leased-warehouse system and the ability to hire carriers, not an unbounded logistics TAM. The conditional base model’s ₹240 crore annualized bridge and 8% growth produce a much larger five-year network requirement. Revenue per branch would have to increase, or branches/routes/customers be added; neither contracted volume nor utilization capacity was disclosed. Consequently the modeled pace is an assumption, not a backlog forecast. The bull requires 15% growth, higher operating margin and faster collections simultaneously. [B01,B04,M01]

The main incremental asset is the customer claim, not just trucks. Base end-receivable days 175, payables 65 days on operating cost, operating advances 3.2% of sales and fixed investment 5.5% of incremental sales are explicit. Maintenance is the greater of 0.9% of revenue and 15% of opening net operating fixed assets annually. Software commitment ₹0.1062 crore is separately funded; existing software advances are not paid twice. Wage/carrier and rent costs are inside EBITDA. A small operating-cash reserve grows with sales and must actually be funded. Capital required for revenue growth is never treated as a source of funds. [M01]

The IPO prospectus estimated FY27 debtor days 160 versus provisional FY26 177, and creditor days 45 versus 66. The apparent benefit of faster collection is partly offset by shorter supplier credit. Planned working-capital IPO proceeds ₹19.7216 crore largely finance this balance-sheet need; general purposes ₹4 crore and issue expenses ₹3.4944 crore are not additional operating earnings. The actual utilization certificate is still a diligence requirement, and the interim cash location cannot be assumed from IPO net proceeds alone. [A06,B04]

GQS raw 5.35 is capped at 5 because CASH3 reflects persistent poor realization during growth. That is not a penalty for an isolated transient receivable build or a duplicate downgrade for capex. Current evidence supports moderate nominal expansion and accounting profit improvement, not high-quality cash-backed compounding. Growth≈reinvestment×incremental return is used only as a consistency check: an 8% growth path at roughly mid-teens incremental returns can consume around half of incremental operating earnings before considering cash reserves and maturities. High payouts and that same growth cannot both be assumed without funding. [C02,C03,M01]

## 8. Management, Governance & Execution

The original audits, rather than only prospectus assurance, were inspected. D D Baheti & Co signed FY21–FY23; SPG Associates signed FY24–FY26. Both records name Deen Dayal, membership 089466. FY24 CARO acknowledges a statutory-auditor resignation but says no issues/objections/concerns were raised. That is not treated as a scope-dispute resignation. SPG’s disclosed September 2024 appointment runs to 2029. September 2026 changes concerned internal/secretarial auditors and the internal auditor becoming CFO, not a newly inferred statutory-auditor resignation. [A01]

FY26 financial and IFC opinions are unmodified; revenue recognition is a key audit matter, not a qualification. CARO reports no debt default, fraud identified or material one-year liquidity uncertainty and says RPT requirements were complied with. These are meaningful favorable findings but not fraud guarantees. FY24/FY25 audit-trail wording says the edit log operated with no tampering while separately describing preservation reporting as inapplicable. FY26 explicitly confirms preservation where enabled. The earlier wording is recorded, not converted into an accusation of missing current audit trails. [A01]

Historical related-party financing deserves attention. Former subsidiary principal and guarantees were large relative to equity. FY24 original CARO includes conflicting language on whether principal/interest repayment schedules were stipulated. By FY25 the disclosed principal loans had disappeared; OSPT’s ₹5.78 crore guarantee was released 7 April 2025. Accrued interest subsequently reached ₹1.7768 crore, but the FY26 note does not name its counterparty. It is therefore wrong both to assume all exposure was collected and to assert all accrued interest still belongs to OSPT. [A03–A05]

FY26 director remuneration ₹0.66 crore is disclosed; the principal family’s property/security/rent and loan transactions are identified. Promoter/group postissue ownership 71.94% is dated to the prospectus/listing basis, not substituted for a verified September pledge report. The prospectus states promoter shares were unpledged then. Nonpromoter residual 28.06% is not necessarily unlocked free float. No broad clean-current-pledge assertion is made. [A05,L01]

## 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path

The strongest bear thesis is that margin expansion reflects attractive-looking recognized freight economics while customer billing/collection persistently lags. Loss of a large customer or carrier repricing can reduce utilization and margins at the same time as debtor days lengthen and suppliers demand earlier settlement. Debt rolls, factoring recourse, tax claims and payroll do not wait for earnings recognition. The resulting need for new capital can force unfavorable dilution within a very small currently authorized share headroom, or require new authorization not assumed here. [A04,B02,M01]

The single most important thesis-break variable is sustained cash realization of the debtor/unbilled book, not the headline order pipeline or quarterly PAT. A temporary price fall does not establish impairment. Evidence of systematically uncollectible billed claims, continued growth in aged unbilled balances without customer acceptance, or inability to fund essential obligations would change the thesis materially. Actual diversion or fabricated recognition would trigger governance/reliability reassessment, but neither is inferred from current gaps. [A01,C02]

Counterevidence is substantial and must not be buried: FY26 financial/IFC audits are unmodified, CARO reports no default or one-year uncertainty, IPO cash is real funding, stated funded leverage is below 2 x EBITDA, operating margins improved, some guarantees were released, and December unbilled balances reduced by March. Those facts argue against declaring the business already distressed. The assessed impairment risk is High under linked operating/funding stress, not a probability estimate or an actual-default claim. Failed-path ordinary returns are NS rather than an invented recovery value. [A01,A03,A06,M01]

The market may already understand SME lot constraints and working-capital intensity. No differentiated-information advantage is claimed merely because the public filings are lengthy or the quote is below a peer multiple. The useful analytical distinction is cash available versus total cash, current versus pre-IPO EPS, and the difference between original and restated tax/cash-flow presentation. [C04,L01]

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.content_markdown: Sampark is an established, predominantly domestic B2B freight coordinator with road, air and rail capabilities, leased warehousing and small emerging international/umbrella services. Its operating margins have improved, but the central investment question is whether invoiced and unbilled revenue can become cash without consuming repeated fresh capital. FY26 revenue was ₹223.2664 crore and operating EBITDA ₹20.0143 crore, yet CFO was only ₹1.8129 crore and genuinely unrestricted cash approximately ₹0.6720 crore. The July 2026 IPO provides meaningful working-capital relief, not proof of a completed improvement in collection economics. Historical BQS is 4.92 (displayed 4.9); raw GQS is 5.35, capped at 5.0 because CASH is 3. IAS remains NS because a supported forward return, price-implied expectation and primary liquidity assessment are unresolved. This is a mixed-quality, cash-constrained logistics watchlist case, not an evidence-backed compounder or an evidenced governance/default failure. At the secondary 19 October close of ₹141.50, valuation work is conditional. Better collections, documented IPO deployment, bank availability and an executable primary trade record could change the assessment. [A04,A06,C01–C04,L01]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.content_markdown:
The operating proposition is coordination and service reliability: collect B2B consignments, consolidate and route them through carriers and branch infrastructure, deliver to the consignee, obtain proof/acceptance, invoice and collect. Sampark offers FTL/LTL road movement, air and rail forwarding, warehousing, inventory handling and packaging. Its prospectus records 50 branches, 56 owned vehicles, and eight leased warehouses totalling 124,500 square feet. Hired pickup/delivery and external carriers are economically important, so owned-vehicle count is not total throughput capacity. Office and warehouse rent stays in operating cost under this Indian GAAP presentation; no invented Ind AS lease liability is added. [B01,B02]

FY26 note 17 reconciles ₹223.2664 crore revenue as net billed freight ₹195.1314 crore, warehousing ₹7.5811 crore, truck/GPS rental ₹0.0007 crore, current unbilled freight ₹18.8828 crore and umbrella supplier revenue ₹1.6704 crore. Gross freight ₹208.7094 crore first reverses prior unbilled ₹13.5780 crore. Therefore ₹18.8828 crore is not all incremental recognition: the net annual unbilled addition is ₹5.3048 crore. The December-to-March fall in the unbilled balance is not automatically cash collection; it can be invoicing or other movement. [B03; FY26 annual printed 65/PDF69]

The older prospectus describes domestic B2B logistics, but FY26 adds international freight and umbrella services. Foreign-exchange umbrella income is ₹1.6703 crore and freight income ₹0.0053 crore; the directors’ total differs by ₹0.0001 crore rounding. “100% domestic” is therefore not carried forward. Current international activity remains small; it is not evidence of a broad international franchise. A single reportable segment is an accounting disclosure, not proof of identical service-level margins. [B01,B03]

Revenue recognition is a FY26 key audit matter. Delivery/control transfer and service performance underpin recognition; invoice approval and customer reconciliation affect timing. There is a genuine sequence from service delivery to billing to collection, and the model keeps billed/unbilled movements separate. Carrier costs and payroll can precede cash receipts, explaining why an apparently asset-light coordinator can be intensely working-capital dependent. [A01,A04,M01]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.content_markdown:
The best proposed mechanism is local network knowledge and integrated customer service: routes, carrier relationships and branch execution can reduce coordination friction. Evidence is a meaningful operating footprint and repeated activity over more than a decade. Durability depends on service retention, route density, passing through freight costs and billing discipline. Failure modes are price-based tender competition, carrier repricing, customer switching and funding an ever-larger debtor book. Neither ISO certification, GPS, reputed customer logos nor high reported ROCE proves a moat. The issuer itself describes fragmented competition and low barriers, and relies on third-party technology and capacity. Proprietary technology is not established. [B01,B02]

Customer concentration is real but not one-customer dependence: FY25 top customer represented 7.82% and top ten 38.72% of sales; nine-month FY26 top customer 9.56%, top ten 34.34%. Supplier concentration is greater: FY25 top supplier 32.23% and top ten 64.17% of operating procurement expenses. These are different denominators. Names of the latest top supplier/customer are not disclosed in those tables. Fretex matches the FY23/FY24 top-customer amounts, ₹16.3136/₹22.6181 crore, when it was related. Nil later related-party sales is not proof sales ceased after its relationship changed. [B02,B03]

Three named economic comparators are retained, not a generic SME basket:

| Orissa Bengal Carrier | CARE’s July 2025 rationale describes 83 owned vehicles, 39 branches, roughly 5,000 hired-vehicle linkages and industrial customers; FY25 turnover ₹304.8924 crore and thin profits. | Closest hybrid domestic-freight comparison, but heavier bulk/industrial orientation. Its 77-day working-capital cycle is not directly comparable to Sampark debtor days. Thin margins show competitive downside. |
| GB Logistics Commerce | FY25 original annual report describes owned/hired FTL capacity and commodity trading; goods are ₹9.2288 crore, 14.23% of ₹64.8531 crore standalone revenue. It also has a subsidiary. | Smaller-scale comparator, but service/trading and consolidation mix prevent mechanical margin/P/E ranking. The issuer-prospectus EPS does not fully reconcile to the original peer EPS note; no current multiple adopted. |

FY25 revenue ₹3,160.948 crore provides a superior scale benchmark, not a direct valuation twin. | The prospectus combines ₹242.66 with pre-bonus ₹20.91 EPS. After the 18 August 2025 1:1 bonus, FY25 EPS is ₹10.46, so that dated diagnostic is about 23.20 x, not 11.60 x. Neither is a current valuation. |

Peer operating evidence comes from original issuer/credit-rating sources; figures reproduced by Sampark’s offer document retain that provenance. Current peer market caps, EV/EBITDA and P/E remain ND rather than invented. The peer source registry includes exact links and page locators, including VRL’s original correction/bonus evidence. A claim that Sampark is cheap against an unadjusted advertised peer multiple is rejected. [B02; peer_inputs.json]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.content_markdown:
A bottom-up scale test starts with the existing 50-branch/56-owned-vehicle/leased-warehouse system and the ability to hire carriers, not an unbounded logistics TAM. The conditional base model’s ₹240 crore annualized bridge and 8% growth produce a much larger five-year network requirement. Revenue per branch would have to increase, or branches/routes/customers be added; neither contracted volume nor utilization capacity was disclosed. Consequently the modeled pace is an assumption, not a backlog forecast. The bull requires 15% growth, higher operating margin and faster collections simultaneously. [B01,B04,M01]

The main incremental asset is the customer claim, not just trucks. Base end-receivable days 175, payables 65 days on operating cost, operating advances 3.2% of sales and fixed investment 5.5% of incremental sales are explicit. Maintenance is the greater of 0.9% of revenue and 15% of opening net operating fixed assets annually. Software commitment ₹0.1062 crore is separately funded; existing software advances are not paid twice. Wage/carrier and rent costs are inside EBITDA. A small operating-cash reserve grows with sales and must actually be funded. Capital required for revenue growth is never treated as a source of funds. [M01]

The IPO prospectus estimated FY27 debtor days 160 versus provisional FY26 177, and creditor days 45 versus 66. The apparent benefit of faster collection is partly offset by shorter supplier credit. Planned working-capital IPO proceeds ₹19.7216 crore largely finance this balance-sheet need; general purposes ₹4 crore and issue expenses ₹3.4944 crore are not additional operating earnings. The actual utilization certificate is still a diligence requirement, and the interim cash location cannot be assumed from IPO net proceeds alone. [A06,B04]

GQS raw 5.35 is capped at 5 because CASH3 reflects persistent poor realization during growth. That is not a penalty for an isolated transient receivable build or a duplicate downgrade for capex. Current evidence supports moderate nominal expansion and accounting profit improvement, not high-quality cash-backed compounding. Growth≈reinvestment×incremental return is used only as a consistency check: an 8% growth path at roughly mid-teens incremental returns can consume around half of incremental operating earnings before considering cash reserves and maturities. High payouts and that same growth cannot both be assumed without funding. [C02,C03,M01]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.content_markdown:
The original audits, rather than only prospectus assurance, were inspected. D D Baheti & Co signed FY21–FY23; SPG Associates signed FY24–FY26. Both records name Deen Dayal, membership 089466. FY24 CARO acknowledges a statutory-auditor resignation but says no issues/objections/concerns were raised. That is not treated as a scope-dispute resignation. SPG’s disclosed September 2024 appointment runs to 2029. September 2026 changes concerned internal/secretarial auditors and the internal auditor becoming CFO, not a newly inferred statutory-auditor resignation. [A01]

FY26 financial and IFC opinions are unmodified; revenue recognition is a key audit matter, not a qualification. CARO reports no debt default, fraud identified or material one-year liquidity uncertainty and says RPT requirements were complied with. These are meaningful favorable findings but not fraud guarantees. FY24/FY25 audit-trail wording says the edit log operated with no tampering while separately describing preservation reporting as inapplicable. FY26 explicitly confirms preservation where enabled. The earlier wording is recorded, not converted into an accusation of missing current audit trails. [A01]

Historical related-party financing deserves attention. Former subsidiary principal and guarantees were large relative to equity. FY24 original CARO includes conflicting language on whether principal/interest repayment schedules were stipulated. By FY25 the disclosed principal loans had disappeared; OSPT’s ₹5.78 crore guarantee was released 7 April 2025. Accrued interest subsequently reached ₹1.7768 crore, but the FY26 note does not name its counterparty. It is therefore wrong both to assume all exposure was collected and to assert all accrued interest still belongs to OSPT. [A03–A05]

FY26 director remuneration ₹0.66 crore is disclosed; the principal family’s property/security/rent and loan transactions are identified. Promoter/group postissue ownership 71.94% is dated to the prospectus/listing basis, not substituted for a verified September pledge report. The prospectus states promoter shares were unpledged then. Nonpromoter residual 28.06% is not necessarily unlocked free float. No broad clean-current-pledge assertion is made. [A05,L01]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.content_markdown:
The strongest bear thesis is that margin expansion reflects attractive-looking recognized freight economics while customer billing/collection persistently lags. Loss of a large customer or carrier repricing can reduce utilization and margins at the same time as debtor days lengthen and suppliers demand earlier settlement. Debt rolls, factoring recourse, tax claims and payroll do not wait for earnings recognition. The resulting need for new capital can force unfavorable dilution within a very small currently authorized share headroom, or require new authorization not assumed here. [A04,B02,M01]

The single most important thesis-break variable is sustained cash realization of the debtor/unbilled book, not the headline order pipeline or quarterly PAT. A temporary price fall does not establish impairment. Evidence of systematically uncollectible billed claims, continued growth in aged unbilled balances without customer acceptance, or inability to fund essential obligations would change the thesis materially. Actual diversion or fabricated recognition would trigger governance/reliability reassessment, but neither is inferred from current gaps. [A01,C02]

Counterevidence is substantial and must not be buried: FY26 financial/IFC audits are unmodified, CARO reports no default or one-year uncertainty, IPO cash is real funding, stated funded leverage is below 2 x EBITDA, operating margins improved, some guarantees were released, and December unbilled balances reduced by March. Those facts argue against declaring the business already distressed. The assessed impairment risk is High under linked operating/funding stress, not a probability estimate or an actual-default claim. Failed-path ordinary returns are NS rather than an invented recovery value. [A01,A03,A06,M01]

The market may already understand SME lot constraints and working-capital intensity. No differentiated-information advantage is claimed merely because the public filings are lengthy or the quote is below a peer multiple. The useful analytical distinction is cash available versus total cash, current versus pre-IPO EPS, and the difference between original and restated tax/cash-flow presentation. [C04,L01]

sections.content_markdown:
Five-year 5× requires 37.97% annualized price growth;10×58.49%. Ten-year 5× requires 17.46%;10×25.89%. Those are price growth requirements, not business revenue forecasts. The model explicitly tests 10/20/30/40/50% sales growth,5/10 years and 6/10 x terminal EBIT under the bull operating setup, recomputing capital, funding, whole-share issuance and final claims. Its multibagger table retains all evaluations, including finance failures. [M02]

Revenue, margins, enterprise value, equity and per-share value are separated. Shareholders do not receive enterprise-value growth free of debt or dilution. Higher volumes require carrier capacity, branches/customer access, receivables, software/maintenance and operating cash. Pricing assumptions cannot simply turn a 56-vehicle footprint into an owned-capacity promise, because outsourced capacity is material. Market share is ND without a defensible accessible-lane denominator. The lower 6 x terminal EBIT case avoids relying exclusively on rerating. [B01,M02]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.content_markdown:
BQS4.92 places the business in the mixed-quality band; final GQS5.0 reflects modest growth quality after the explicit cash cap. IAS is NS, so the price-dependent matrix cannot be assigned a numeric investment cell. G4 is a research hold for unresolved implementation evidence, not a finding the stock is suspended or untradeable. No evidence-backed compounder designation is permissible because BQS/GQS and required moat/cash factors do not meet the thresholds. [C01–C04,L01]

Action: research watchlist, not eligible for an unqualified purchase conclusion. Priorities are current cash/funding verification, collection/interest-asset evidence, restatement clarification and a usable primary trade record. A lower price alone does not resolve those gaps, and price-linked equity funding must be re-solved rather than scaled mechanically. An existing shareholder faces an implementation and thesis-monitoring question; without their holdings/tax context no reduce/exit instruction is given. No trade has been executed. [M01,M02,L01]

Positive future operating evidence can raise BQS/GQS; a price move alone changes only price-sensitive assessment. Reported failures in a deliberately conservative financing path are not automatically G3 Fail. Conversely, a source-qualified clean audit does not guarantee collection or future funding. This distinction keeps a useful caution from becoming an unsupported allegation.

ND means unavailable/not located; NM means economically meaningless; NA truly inapplicable; NS not scoreable. “V” verifies a disclosure, “M” identifies a management assertion, “C” an auditable calculation and “A” an analyst assumption. Full future finance, timing, operating reserve, capex, tax-rate and terminal assumptions are in model_inputs.json/model_spec.md. No assumption is disguised as bank commitment or observed October financials.

Open questions with greatest decision impact: (1) How much IPO cash remains, where, and with what eligibility restrictions? (2) What are current bank drawing powers, repayment dates and rollover terms? (3) What customer/counterparty evidence supports aged/unbilled and accrued-interest recoverability? (4) Why does the subsequent statutory presentation revert to pre-restatement FY25 deferred tax, and what explains FY23 opening reserves? (5) What are current promoter encumbrance/lock-in and executable primary trading conditions? (6) What unit volumes, prices and lane/customer economics underlie revenue expansion?
